topic: Weekly regime and daily market structure
evidence: Creator description, chapter and companion episode transcript
lesson: A move through a daily level can matter to traders on several horizons. Look for agreement across horizons when judging a setup.
hypothesis: For continuation, label the last completed week bullish when its close exceeds its 10-week SMA and that average rose from the prior week. Reverse both comparisons for bearish. Otherwise label mixed and wait.
requires: Completed weekly closes, including the prior average. Never use Friday's eventual close earlier in that week.

source.title: How to Use Multi-Timeframe Analysis & Find the Best Trading Setups
source.author: TheOneLanceB
source.evidence_type: Creator companion explanation

topic: Long breakout and short breakdown from a range
evidence: Creator chapter on continuation, with breakout and breakdown named in the swing lessons companion episode
lesson: Continuation is one of Lance's two swing setup families. The working premise is that price will keep moving in the direction of the break.
hypothesis: In a bullish weekly regime, flag a long when today's completed close exceeds the highest high of the prior 20 sessions. In a bearish regime, flag a short below the lowest low of those sessions. Record range width divided by ATR before the break so tight and wide bases can be compared.
requires: Completed daily OHLC and weekly regime. Equality or a wick through the level alone leaves the candidate flat.

topic: Mean reversion after capitulation or upside exhaustion
evidence: Creator chapter on mean reversion, with multi-day capitulation discussed in the swing lessons companion episode
lesson: Mean reversion is a separate swing setup family. A multi-day extreme can be the context for a reversal.
hypothesis: On day D, flag a downside stretch if the close is at least two prior ATRs below the prior 20-session SMA. Require D+1 to close above D's high before flagging a long. Mirror the stretch and confirmation for a short. An unconfirmed stretch expires after D+1.
requires: Comparable split-adjusted OHLC, completed confirmation bar and warmed indicators. Tag weekly regime for analysis. Conflicting continuation and reversal signals on the same close mean wait.

source.author: TheOneLanceB
source.evidence_type: Creator syndicated chapter notes

topic: Relative volume, volatility and trend indicators
evidence: Creator chapter showing multi-timeframe trade examples. Indicator definitions below are research choices.
lesson: Compare how the same setup appears on different chart horizons.
hypothesis: Use SMA for trend, ATR for comparable distances, and relative daily volume for participation. Compare each feature with a price-only baseline. Relative volume is today's downloaded daily share volume divided by the mean of the prior 20 valid consecutive sessions. Leave missing or zero-denominator ratios unknown.
requires: Use mean true range over 14 completed sessions for this pilot. Each true range is the maximum of high minus low and the absolute gaps from prior close to high or low. Keep provider bar volume separate from observed counter deltas.

source.title: How to Use Multi-Timeframe Analysis & Find the Best Trading Setups
source.author: TheOneLanceB
source.evidence_type: Creator companion explanation

topic: Overnight gap risk, stops and position sizing
evidence: Creator chapter and companion episode transcript
lesson: A swing trade can require a wider structural stop and can open beyond that stop. Carrying intraday share size overnight changes the exposure.
hypothesis: For continuation use the breakout day's low as the long stop or high as the short stop. For reversal use the stretch day's extreme. At entry use shares = floor(dollar risk budget / (max(structural stop distance, adverse gap stress per share) + round-trip cost allowance per share)). Round shares down. Skip invalid stops or zero shares.
requires: Entry price, stop on the loss side, positive gap stress, risk budget, estimated costs and buying power. A stressed loss estimate is not a maximum loss.

topic: Portfolio buying power and competing positions
evidence: Creator chapter and companion episode transcript
lesson: A multi-day position consumes buying power that may be needed for a better opportunity. Evaluate new ideas alongside existing positions.
hypothesis: Cap proposed shares by available buying power and remaining portfolio risk. For a short also require confirmed borrow availability, borrow cost and margin. Return wait with the missing input or binding constraint.
requires: Timestamped account snapshot, open positions and declared exposure limits. Arbitrade's current paper account supports long inventory only.

topic: Trend direction from swing highs and swing lows
evidence: Creator companion article
lesson: Successive rising peaks and troughs describe an uptrend. Falling peaks and troughs describe a downtrend. A sideways sequence has no clear direction.
hypothesis: Annotate the last two confirmed peaks and troughs with their confirmation times. Classify mixed sequences as indeterminate. Compare pivot direction with the weekly filter before proposing continuation.
requires: Sufficient left and right history to confirm each pivot as of the decision. Mark an emerging pivot provisional.

topic: Wait in chop inside a range
evidence: Creator companion article
lesson: Repeated entries inside a directionless range can accumulate losses before a meaningful break occurs.
hypothesis: Mark the two boundaries before reviewing the latest bar. In the interior, return wait on a breakout thesis. A failed probe back inside is evidence against continuation.
requires: Both range edges and an uncropped history. A tight range alone supplies no direction.

hypothesis: Record the level before the trigger, the earlier reactions, and where candles closed after each test. If a wide price zone allows either interpretation, mark the level ambiguous.
requires: Readable price scale and earlier tests. A line drawn by a user is an annotation, not independent evidence.

hypothesis: For a candidate bounce, compare the close after a reclaim with the earlier falling leg. Record the extreme and the reclaim separately. A green bar in an ongoing decline is insufficient on its own.
requires: Ordered completed bars on the setup horizon, an identifiable extreme and a predeclared confirmation rule.
